latest_release.name: Open PDF Studio v2026.48.1
latest_release.body:
## What's new in 2026.48.1

- Embed installed fonts selected by their localized family names, including individual faces in font collections.
- Desktop search uses the same text extraction as the web viewer for more consistent results on rotated text and subset fonts. Supported desktop builds can embed large PNG images through Rust; smaller images and unsupported inputs use the JavaScript path.
- Reduced the repository and desktop distribution footprint by removing duplicate test drawings, unused viewer assets and tracked build output.
- Android packages require a fixed release signing key so future builds can retain their update identity.

<!-- openaec-memory-at-rest -->
### OpenAEC Linux

Memory at rest (Linux AppImage, no document open, software rendering): 374 MiB PSS over 7 processes

### Verification

The signed Windows portable package opened and zoomed all 41 verification PDFs in the visible desktop application. Median times were 3.438 s to open and 0.531 s to zoom. The slowest measurements were 8.485 s and 2.031 s respectively. The Windows user installer has a valid Authenticode signature.

Live reviews are excluded. Existing snapshot review functionality remains available. TypeScript checks passed. The local JavaScript test suites passed 9,008 tests and skipped 29.

Windows, macOS and Linux desktop builds succeeded. This release has no Android APK because the permanent signing credentials were unavailable. The optional Flatpak build failed because its source directory lies outside the manifest directory.

**English** · [Nederlands](README.nl.md)
# Open PDF Studio **A free, open-source PDF editor for people who work with drawings: markup, measuring to scale, revision compare and CAD import, on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and in the browser.** [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio?label=release&color=D97706)](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/releases/latest) [![CI](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-LGPL--3.0--or--later-blue)](#license) [![Languages](https://img.shields.io/badge/languages-40-informational)](open-pdf-studio/js/i18n/locales/) [![MCP tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/MCP%20tools-96-informational)](mcp-stdio/tools.json) ### [Try in your browser](https://open-pdf-studio.open-aec.com/)  ·  [Download](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/releases/latest) ![A floor plan with a revision cloud, a callout and a measured distance; the Format tab and the properties of the selected callout are open](docs/images/readme/hero.png)
Open PDF Studio is a PDF editor for architects, engineers, contractors and everyone else who reviews drawings and documents. You mark up, measure with the scale the drawing carries, compare revisions, place symbols, count quantities and organise pages, with no subscription, account or watermark. It runs as a desktop app on Windows, macOS and Linux, as an Android app, and in your browser with nothing to install. The desktop app adds what needs your computer: printing, OCR, DWG and DXF import and export, digital signatures and a local AI connection (MCP). ## Try it **[Open the browser version](https://open-pdf-studio.open-aec.com/)** and open a PDF from your computer. You get the same ribbon, markup, measuring, compare, symbol and page tools as in the desktop app. Your document stays in your browser and is not uploaded; a page reload starts empty. Buttons for desktop-only features are switched off and say why. ## Download Every release is on the [releases page](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/releases/latest). | Platform | Files | |----------|-------| | **Windows** | `…_x64-setup.exe` (all users, needs admin), `…_x64_user-setup.exe` (current user only), `…_x64_portable.zip` (no install, [details](docs/portable-windows.md)) | | **macOS** | `…_universal.dmg` (Apple silicon and Intel, macOS 10.15 or later) | | **Linux** | `.deb`, `.AppImage` and `.snap` for x86_64, also in the [Snap Store](https://snapcraft.io/open-pdf-studio); Nix flake. See [docs/install-linux.md](docs/install-linux.md) | | **Android** | `open-pdf-studio-release.apk` (64-bit ARM) | | **Other** | `open-pdf-studio.mcpb` (AI connection for MCP clients), `open-pdf-studio-web-.tar.gz` (web version to host yourself), winget manifests, the Python library (`.whl` and `.tar.gz`) | ### Downloads in numbers How often the installers on the releases page were downloaded. | Platform | All releases | Latest release | Share | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Windows | 26,905 | 875 | 60.4% | | macOS | 3,483 | 83 | 7.8% | | Linux | 7,386 | 162 | 16.6% | | Android | 6,800 | 144 | 15.3% | | **Total** | **44,574** | **1,264** | **100%** | ```mermaid pie showData title Installer downloads by platform "Windows" : 26905 "macOS" : 3483 "Linux" : 7386 "Android" : 6800 ``` Counted on 2026-11-17 over 89 releases; the latest is v2026.47.0. Only installers count, not the updates an installed copy fetches. The Snap Store, Flathub and the web version are not in these numbers. Update with `node open-pdf-studio/scripts/download-stats.mjs`. **Updates.** The Windows installers, the macOS app, the `.deb` and the AppImage check for updates and install them through the built-in updater, which only accepts updates signed with the project's update key. The snap updates through the Snap Store. The portable version and the Android app do not update themselves. **Signing.** The Windows installers and the program files they install are Authenticode-signed with Azure Trusted Signing; the release workflow installs the signed installer and checks every signature. The macOS app is signed with a Developer ID and notarized by Apple; the workflow checks it with `codesign`, `spctl` and `stapler`. From the first release after 2026.45.0 (the signing job came later), the `.deb`, the AppImage and the snap each have a detached OpenPGP signature (`.asc`) of the OpenAEC Foundation release key, fingerprint `13F6D414ADEE4ED4CD09AC60601D86C93C504D29`, and `SHA256SUMS` with `SHA256SUMS.asc` covers the Linux files; check them with `gpg --verify .asc ` against [`docs/keys/openaec-signing-public-key.asc`](docs/keys/openaec-signing-public-key.asc) (see [docs/install-linux.md](docs/install-linux.md#verifying-the-download-openpgp)). The `.sig` files are the update signatures that the built-in updater checks. The Android APK is signed, but with a new key for every release (see [Current limitations](#current-limitations)). The portable zip and the web bundle come with a `.sha256` file. ## Why use it? - **Free and open.** LGPL-3.0-or-later. No licence fees, no account, no telemetry and no watermark ([PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md)). - **Made for drawings.** Clouds, callouts, hatches, stamps and symbol libraries, and printing to scale on sheets up to A0. - **Measure to scale at once.** A drawing that carries its own scale, such as a CAD plot or an imported DWG, measures correctly without calibrating. - **See what changed.** Compare two revisions side by side or on top of each other, with a list of every change. - **CAD in and out.** Import DWG and DXF as a vector PDF with layers and a measuring scale, and export a page back to DXF or DWG (desktop). - **Works with an AI assistant.** A local MCP server with 96 tools lets an assistant open, mark up, measure and save documents for you (desktop). - **Everywhere.** Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and the browser, in 40 languages. ## Screenshots | | | |---|---| | ![Area, perimeter and two distances measured on a floor plan at scale 1:50, Default theme](docs/images/readme/measure.png) **Measuring with the scale of the drawing** | ![Two revisions of a floor plan on top of each other, with the moved wall highlighted and a list of 18 changes](docs/images/readme/compare.png) **Comparing two revisions** | | ![Fire safety symbols from the NEN 1414 library placed on a floor plan, with the symbol palette open](docs/images/readme/symbols.png) **Symbols from the palette** | ![The Edit Pages window with six pages: a cover, two floor plans and three pages of text](docs/images/readme/pages.png) **Organising pages** | | ![Search results for "wall" in the text and the annotations, theme Dark](docs/images/readme/search.png) **Searching text and annotations, theme Dark** | ![The View tab with the window split in two: a floor plan on the left and the specification on the right, theme Blue](docs/images/readme/split.png) **Split view, theme Blue** | The screenshots come from the browser version with demo PDFs that the script makes itself: `open-pdf-studio/scripts/generate-readme-screenshots.mjs`. ## Markup and measuring - **Markup.** Highlights, shapes, clouds, callouts, text boxes, sticky notes, freehand, stamps, images and signatures, with styles, layers and alignment tools. - **Measuring.** Distance, area, perimeter and angle, to the scale in the drawing or a scale you calibrate, with snapping to the drawing. - **Quantities.** Count objects by category and collect counts, lengths and areas in a schedule that you place on the page or export as CSV. - **Redaction.** Removes the text, images and vectors under the marked area from the file, not just from view. The full list is in [docs/features.md](docs/features.md). ## Documents and pages - **Pages.** Insert, delete, extract, split, rotate, reorder and merge; straighten a skewed scan or shift page content. - **Forms, bookmarks and attachments.** Fill and create form fields, edit bookmarks, manage attachments. - **Watermarks, headers and footers** with page numbers and dates. - **Search** in the page text and in annotations, with a result list per page. - **Keyboard shortcuts** that you can change, including a preset with single-letter markup keys: [docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md](docs/keyboard-shortcuts.md). ## Desktop features - **CAD.** DWG and DXF import with layers, viewports and a measuring scale, and export of a page to DXF or DWG. - **Printing** to scale on large sheets, with a live preview and *Save as PDF*. - **OCR** to make scans searchable. - **Digital signatures**: validation with the certificate chain, and signing. - **Managed installs** with `OPENAEC_BEHEERD=1` and a fixed start folder: [docs/managed-deployments.md](docs/managed-deployments.md). ## Interoperability | Format | Open / import | Save / export | |--------|---------------|---------------| | **PDF** | Yes, including forms (AcroForm, XFA) and layers | Yes; PDF/A validation and saving, PDF/X export, raster PDF, flattened copy | | **XFDF** | Annotations; a tool set from sample markups | Annotations | | **BCF 2.1** | Issues as annotations | Annotations as issues | | **DWG, DXF** | Yes, as a vector PDF (desktop) | A page with its layers and markups (desktop) | | **IFCX** (IFC5 JSON) | No | Yes, beta ([docs/ifcx-export.md](docs/ifcx-export.md)) | | **PNG, JPEG** | As an image on a page | Pages, at 72 to 600 DPI | | **DOCX, ODT, XLSX** | No | Text and tables | | **CSV** | Edited tags of a saved quantities schedule (label, IFC category, location, count category) | Quantities schedule, with an ID column per markup | What does not survive: XFDF and BCF carry annotations only, not the page content. A flattened copy leaves out form field values. DOCX, ODT and XLSX get the text and tables, and complex layouts may need correction. PDF/X keeps standard fonts that are not embedded as they are. What IFCX keeps and loses is listed in [docs/ifcx-export.md](docs/ifcx-export.md). ## Embedding in a web page A separate, lightweight build lets another web application show a drawing with measuring and comments in its own page: `npm run build:web-unit` writes `open-pdf-studio/dist-web-unit/`. The script a host loads is about 10 KiB gzip; PDF.js arrives with the first document, the PDF writer only when the host asks for the result, and nothing in the unit uses the desktop shell. It uses the same annotation model as the desktop app, so a drawing marked up on the web opens the same way on the desktop. ```html
``` The same unit works as a `` element and inside an iframe with a `postMessage` protocol. Options include a read-only mode (`readOnly: true`), a dark theme and CSS variables, a hidden toolbar for hosts with their own buttons, and `storage: 'local'` to remember the page and scale per document (off by default). The events are `opds:load`, `opds:change`, `opds:save` and `opds:error`. A minimal host page is in [`open-pdf-studio/web-unit/voorbeeld/`](open-pdf-studio/web-unit/voorbeeld/index.html). The unit measures distances and places sticky notes and rectangles; area, perimeter, text boxes, editing existing annotations and XFDF are not in it yet ([#451](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/451)). ## MCP The desktop app has a built-in MCP server, so an AI assistant can work with your documents: open and save files, navigate, create and edit annotations, set the measuring scale, take off quantities, import and export CAD and print to a PDF file. It has 96 public tools. You stay in control. The server is on for a new installation and listens only on your own computer (`127.0.0.1`, port 9223); switch it off or change the port under Settings > General. The status bar shows when an assistant is connected and which tool it used last. `open-pdf-studio.mcpb` from the release installs the connection in MCP clients that support `.mcpb` bundles; [mcp-stdio/README.md](mcp-stdio/README.md) explains the bridge for other clients. A [Python library](docs/python-library.md) drives the same tools from a script. **Where your document goes.** The MCP connection itself stays on your computer, but the assistant you connect decides where the work is done. If it uses an online AI service, the page text, screenshots and annotations it reads through the tools can be sent to that service. Check that service's data terms before you let it work on confidential drawings, or use an assistant with a model that runs locally. ## Testing and reliability - **798 unit test files** run with `npm run test:unit` on Windows, Linux and macOS in [CI](.github/workflows/ci.yml) for every pull request, plus 3 quality regression test files (`npm run test:quality`). - **CI builds the app on all three desktop platforms** and starts it: the AppImage on Debian 13, Fedora 44 and in OpenAEC Linux conditions, and the macOS app. It also tests the Python library, lints the Flatpak when it changes, and loads the hosted web bundle in headless Chromium under a strict content security policy. - **Pull requests that touch rendering** also run a render regression on a large-format drawing and keep the report ([render-regression.yml](.github/workflows/render-regression.yml)). - **Releases are checked before they are published.** The release workflow installs the signed Windows installer and checks every signature, starts the portable zip, verifies the macOS signature, notarization and start-up, and verifies the OpenPGP signatures of the Linux packages against the public key in the repository. - **Privacy is tested.** A unit test fails when the shipped source contains an internet address that [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) does not list, or when a telemetry package is added. - **README images are checked.** `node open-pdf-studio/scripts/check-readme-images.mjs` fails when an image is missing, unused or larger than 150 kB. Count sources: unit test files are the non-comment lines of [`open-pdf-studio/scripts/unit-testlijst.txt`](open-pdf-studio/scripts/unit-testlijst.txt); quality tests are the `test:quality` script in [`open-pdf-studio/package.json`](open-pdf-studio/package.json); MCP tools are the entries in [`mcp-stdio/tools.json`](mcp-stdio/tools.json); languages are the folders in [`open-pdf-studio/js/i18n/locales/`](open-pdf-studio/js/i18n/locales/). ## Current limitations - **Linux packages up to 2026.44.8 render without the worker pool.** They lacked the `pdfium-worker` sidecar, so every page rendered in-process and large documents were slow ([#923](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/923)). The fix is on `main` and ships with the next release. - **On some Linux systems the app can still crash while zooming.** The app now lowers the realtime limit and turns off GPU acceleration of the page canvas, the two known causes; the issue stays open until that is confirmed on affected systems ([#924](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/924), workarounds in [docs/install-linux.md](docs/install-linux.md)). - **An Android update does not install over the previous version.** Every release signs the APK with a new key, so Android refuses the update; uninstall the old version first ([#601](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/601)). The Android app has no OCR and renders with PDF.js. - **The browser version has no desktop features.** Printing, OCR, CAD import and export, compression, PDF/X, IFC export, document protection, extensions, updates, the MCP server and signature validation need the desktop app. - **Some virus scanners flag the Windows installer.** The installers are signed, but a new release has little reputation with the virus scanner built into Windows and similar scanners at first ([#761](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/761), [docs/windows-distribution.md](docs/windows-distribution.md)). - **Printing to some third-party virtual PDF printers crashes that printer's own program** ([#699](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/699)). - **Only x86_64 on Windows and Linux.** A Windows on ARM build exists only as an experimental workflow, there is no `.rpm`, and the Flatpak is not on Flathub yet ([docs/flathub.md](docs/flathub.md)). - **The Table button on the Drawing tab is not available yet.** Place a quantities schedule as a table instead. Found something? [Open an issue](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues). ## Under the hood The app is a [Tauri 2](https://tauri.app/) desktop app with a Rust back end and a [SolidJS](https://www.solidjs.com/) front end built with [Vite](https://vitejs.dev/). Pages render through a multi-process [PDFium](https://pdfium.googlesource.com/pdfium/) worker pool, off the UI thread and isolated from crashes, with progressive tiles for very large drawings; the browser and Android versions render with [PDF.js](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/), which also provides the text layer. [pdf-lib](https://pdf-lib.js.org/) writes the PDF changes. The browser version is the same front end built without the Tauri shell. The licences of all components are in [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md). ### Rust and speed Heavy work moves from JavaScript to Rust step by step, each step with a parity test and a measurement. The chart shows the share of Rust in the project's own code over the last six months, and the measured time of a number of operations before and after they were optimised. ![Left: the share of Rust in the own code grew from 16% in May to 28% in November 2026. Right: measured times before and after, from 1.7 to 38 times faster](docs/images/readme/code-and-speed.svg) The lines are counted on `main` at the middle of each month, without tests and vendored code. The times come from [docs/rust-stappen.md](docs/rust-stappen.md) and [docs/performance/](docs/performance/); they were measured in October and November 2026, each pair on the same machine. The app's own code grew fourfold in the same period, so the share says where new work lands, not that JavaScript shrank. ### Code in numbers Lines of code in this repository, counted over the tracked files. Bundled third-party code and generated files are left out; Rust keeps its unit tests inside the source files. | Language | Source lines | Test lines | Total | Share | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | JavaScript / TypeScript | 316,143 | 136,426 | 452,569 | 80.7% | | Rust | 104,402 | 3,879 | 108,281 | 19.3% | | **Total** | **420,545** | **140,305** | **560,850** | **100%** | ```mermaid pie showData title Lines of code by language "JavaScript / TypeScript (source)" : 316143 "JavaScript / TypeScript (tests)" : 136426 "Rust (source)" : 104402 "Rust (tests)" : 3879 ``` Update with `node open-pdf-studio/scripts/code-stats.mjs`. ## Contributing - **Report a bug or ask for a feature** as an [issue](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio/issues/new). Describe what you did, what you expected and what happened. Because the code moves quickly, a precise issue is often more useful than a pull request. - **Share symbol libraries and other content.** Pull requests with symbol sets, hatch patterns and similar content from your country or discipline are very welcome. - **Write code.** Read [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) first. We are looking for someone to maintain the extensions and the content repository: curating incoming symbol libraries and keeping the catalogue organised. If that is you, open an issue to introduce yourself. ## Quick start (developers) ```bash git clone https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation/open-pdf-studio.git cd open-pdf-studio/open-pdf-studio npm ci npm run tauri:dev ``` Requires Node.js 22, Rust stable, CMake and a C/C++ toolchain, plus the WebKitGTK development packages on Linux. Details, release builds, the web version and tests are in [docs/building.md](docs/building.md). Versions follow the OpenAEC scheme `YYYY.W.N`: year, ISO week without a leading zero, and a number within the week that starts at 0, such as `2026.44.8`. Open PDF Studio is part of the [OpenAEC Foundation](https://github.com/OpenAEC-Foundation) family of apps. ## License Open PDF Studio is licensed under the [GNU Lesser General Public License v3.0 or later](LICENSE.md). The LGPL builds on the [GNU General Public License v3.0](GPL-3.0.txt), whose text ships alongside it. [LICENSING.md](LICENSING.md) explains what that means in plain language, lists the licence of every component and of the third-party components the app ships with, and answers the AGPL question around the MuPDF dependency.
